utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon to everybody. Please be seated. My apologies for the late arrivals. I hope they can show good cause for this. It was only yesterday in the evening that the United Nations headquarters in New York announced that opposed to that what we find in writing in all our calendars, Eid al Adha, the Muslim festival of sacrifice, will not be the 12th of February but the 11th of February. This means that no doubt 11th of February, we'll have to follow the rules, will be a day where we can't have any hearings. On the other hand, it was discussed with the parties and there were made a lot of arrangements for the 12th through 14th of February, and it remains with this schedule. In order to have a slight -- at least a slight balance, we will sit on Monday, the 10th of February, from 9.00 to 12.00 and from 1.30 to 4.30. February the 7th was a long story about the possibilities at the end of the day in order to have at least half a day, complete a half day. The hearing will take place from quarter past 2.00 until 7.00 on February -- 7th of February. I'm sorry for these last-minute changes. I know this should have been arranged in a better way, but please be assured that even when we discussed problems related to this week in the Bureau yesterday, nobody knew about this change.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. Good afternoon. We do have a comment. We'd like to address the scheduling problem. And since this is the first time that it arises in connection with the date of February 11th, the Defence would like to make an application at a time when it's convenient for the Court in connection with February 10th and the unavailability of witnesses to proceed on that date as well as Defence counsel. I'm not sure if this is the right time.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I just interrupt you. I wanted to announce this out of the period of time when we have the hearing. But when we enter into details, please let us first call the case and the appearances and then go into details. I wanted to make this announcement previously. Okay. Please.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: Good afternoon. This is case number IT-97-24-T, the Prosecutor versus Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And the appearances for the Prosecution., please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. Nicholas Koumjian, Ann Sutherland, and Ruth Karper.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Your Honours. For the Defence, Branko Lukic, John Ostojic, and Danilo Cirkovic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Then, please, you may continue with your comments related to the schedule.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. In the past practice, I think the Honourable Court has suggested that if there are any problems, we should immediately advise the Court of that or note our objection relating to any scheduling that proceeds. In that vein, we would like to discuss that issue and the Defence would like the opportunity in detail unless the Court prefers to present it in writing, our schedule for the remaining witnesses and what the Defence envisions when those witnesses will be called. The Defence also, in light of the deadline of March 3rd set by the Court last week relating to our expert reports and 92 bis statements, among other things, we believe that it would be beneficial and we would ask respectfully the Court to have that Monday off as well so that we could finalise those documents of both Mr. Lukic and the rest of the Defence team who will be travelling to Prijedor and the surrounding area to complete the 92 bis witnesses. I will be meeting with our experts in the United States in order to complete their review of documents and analysis so that we could timely submit that to the Court. So we would apply orally, unless the Court requires it to be in writing, that we also have Monday, the 10th of February off and not work that day. It would give the Defence an extra weekend to travel to distances that are somewhat far so that we can complete and efficiently conclude --

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Could the counsel slow down, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So that we can complete efficiently the remainder of the Defence case. We've envisioned that there is ample time and there will not be a request to go beyond the prior scheduled deadline that the Court set for the Defence case.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have heard your message. May I hear submissions by the OTP on this issue. My understanding is that there are no objections related to February the 7th, sitting in the afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: There's no formal objection. Just so that the Court is aware, we only have three witnesses that are available to come during that week. The following week, assuming the Court grants our request for the 10th, the following week, the 17th, we envision, obviously with leave of Court, to proceed with the videolink testimony of five witnesses, and we've set forth in an application that will be submitted to the Court tomorrow morning specifically the reasons why these five individuals are unable to come in person but will be seeking leave to present them via videolink. So Friday, the 7th is okay with the Defence so long as the Court does recognise the fact that we only have three witnesses scheduled for that week. We think it will -- it will be completed during that week. We just don't know how soon or if it will take a shorter period than the complete week.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's no doubt -- I gave you immediately the floor. But I think we can't proceed in this way. We already told you the number of remaining witnesses and the remaining days. This be from now on only 30 days. And, therefore, we can't afford any additional day off, and we do what we can do to give the Defence the possibility to present their case, and we are fighting for not only days but for hours, and therefore, to be honest, I can't understand why the intention is to present only three witnesses for next week, knowing that we have the entire day at our disposal for the next week. And as I said previously, at the end of the day, well, say, the 21st of February, we will conclude. And it's a risk for the Defence, but we do what we can to give you the opportunity. And, therefore, please try to call an additional witness for next week. I'm quite sure that it will be possible based on the short statements only to hear more than three witnesses when we sit the entire day throughout the week save for Friday. Regards -- as regards the 10th and 11th, it was scheduled, and we were not aware and also the Defence couldn't be aware that there would be this change, and therefore no doubt it was envisaged also from the side of the Defence to hear witnesses the 10th and the 11th in order to allow at least one witness to be heard that day. Deliberately we tried and successfully we did so to have the 10th of February as one day. What's now with this video conferences. If you can manage it, I would be absolutely surprised because it was only the beginning of this week that I told the parties that the preparation of such a videolink would necessarily take three to four weeks. And based on this, it seems to be impossible -- Madam Registrar may correct me if I'm wrong -- to start a videolink in the week starting with the 17th of February. So --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There's an absolute minimum of two weeks in order to prepare a videolink.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this would be impossible to proceed this way.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The Defence envisioned, Your Honour, to answer a couple of your questions, that by filing an application today or tomorrow that it would give the adequate 14-day notice for video depositions or video testimony to proceed on the 17th of February or at any time thereafter. If it's necessary, we can and would, obviously with the Court's permission, switch some witnesses so that the video depositions proceed on the following week. However, just so that the Court can fully understand the Defence's position on this, we believe that spending some time in the field with witnesses that have become reluctant to testify on behalf of the Defence, for unexplained reasons, that they would possibly come back and testify, would be ready and willing to testify when they have personal contact, as opposed to telephone contact, with the Defence attorneys. Secondly, we believe that in looking at the schedule, although the Court identified a certain 34 number of witnesses remaining, the Defence is prepared sometime after today's hearing to present to the Court a revised list which reduces those number of witnesses. The Defence will in lieu of that present 92 bis statements that we are confident will not require any cross-examination but certainly will defer to the OTP and their opinion of that. We'd also need the time to prepare and to schedule for those 92 bis witnesses and would also, since the registrar will be present during the videolink presentation, in the area would also have that certification complete during the week of the 17th, which would meet the Court's deadline of March 3rd.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: As said before, two weeks is the absolute minimum. And when we discussed it previously or deliberately I said "three to four weeks" because this is more or less the practice. And we had already one example. And then in addition, we need some time for the decision whether to accept video witness or 92 bis statements because it might be that the Chamber may be based on statements by the Prosecution or aproprio motu it comes to the condition that the witness might be of such importance that the only possibility to hear this witness as live witness. We always apply the rule of the best possible evidence, and this means that in some cases a mere videolink is not enough. Maybe also the Defence is aware of the shortcomings and the problems we faced when having heard the video testimony of a Prosecution witness. So, therefore, please be aware that it's not automatic procedure and first we have to hear the Prosecution; and second, we have to decide ourselves. So from the point of view of today, it's impossible to start with links, with a video hearing the 17th of February. But let us hear also the other side. Maybe there are additional arguments or mitigating arguments from the side of the Prosecution.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we don't have an objection to the Monday that counsel is asking about, with the proviso that the representation of the Defence, that they will finish the case on time. I do know that sometimes in preparation, having time to prepare, we can stream line a case and it can go quicker. We in our Prosecution case did not call 16 witnesses that we originally envisioned for one reason or another. As to the 92 bis, I agree completely with Your Honour, and would just -- although we -- there may be many witnesses, we do not need to cross-examine, the minimum requirement for a witness to be eligible is that their testimony will not go to the acts and conduct of the accused. And at least many of the 65 ter summaries that we have would indicate that the witness's testimony would go to the acts and conduct of the accused. But we're certainly willing to consider it. We're willing to cooperate with the Defence. I certainly understand the need of counsel to speak to the witnesses. And we want to be cooperative and flexible with the understanding that they have indicated they will complete the case within the time limit that the Court specified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think nothing has to be added related to video conferences because also here is a question that has to be decided on the basis of what will be expected from these witnesses, whether or not we need the direct contact. I don't want to make reference to the jurisprudence on domestic levels where it's always said that there is such a hierarchy that the best possible and the best available witness is always a witness, when it's -- in case it's an important witness, to be heard in court and not outside and not via video. We are all aware of the shortcomings of a mere video testimony. And if need may be, as already indicated beforehand, in such cases an alternative would be to take depositions, maybe even depositions by the Judges in, be it, Prijedor, Banja Luka, or wherever you tell us the witnesses are residing in the moment. So in conclusion, the 7th, no doubt there will be a hearing in the afternoon as well and we invite the Defence to call another witness for Friday, the 7th. What about the 10th of February? That has to be discussed by the Judges after deliberations during one of the next breaks, and we will announce the outcome later this day. Anything else to be added in the moment before we start with the witness?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Just to inform the Court that we did distribute to the registrar and Defence today colour copies of S394 or a coloured copy for the Court and submitted a revised translation with the correction of the date of S77. I believe, if I remember right, that was -- it's dated 1993, and Your Honours and the Defence pointed out that the correct date on the original was 1992.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do have a comment --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And also S377, the translation is now available and was distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I do object, Your Honour, to the submission of documents that the -- that the OTP claims have been revised. We saw that in fact a document that was translated based upon a video transcript of a witness testifying, that the translator or the interpreters identified the individual as the president. Subsequent to that, we were given a document which apparently made some modifications to it. It's my understanding once evidence is submitted and accepted by the Court, that we cannot just unilaterally or collectively, whether it be the OTP or the Defence, start substituting documents. If the position is of the Defence that the OTP at one time thought Mico Kovacevic was the president and led a certain meeting and that their very own documents from the video transcripts suggest that, and in fact more than suggests that, affirmatively states that, they cannot once we make that known to the Court start replacing documents in evidence. What I would propose respectfully is if there are these, what they would call, typographical errors, that they make an application in writing and keep the original document as admitted, as submitted by them, and then also if permitted by the Court admit the document that they claim has now been corrected. Because the Defence view is that the interpretation of many of the documents are not correct and that it is not a question of a mere typographical error such as the year that was pointed out but the sum and substance of many of these documents, we state and will establish for the Court in due time, have been in fact somewhat distorted. So I would object strongly to the OTP merely handing documents to the registry and simply telling us that they've corrected these typos or alleged typos. These are substantive errors and these are substantive positions that the OTP took in other cases, and we'd like to show the Court the position that they have taken inconsistent with what their position in our view is in this case. And we think that that's significant and that they should not be permitted to do that and that a record should be maintained specifically when in fact they attempt to replace or substitute documents already in evidence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, I don't believe the Defence would like us to request written motions for any correction of the translation of testimony which the Defence has frequently asked for. These corrections are done by CLSS. And as for any error by a Prosecution translator or by a CLSS translator, our -- what members of the OTP believe the facts to be is not evidence. The evidence is coming from witnesses and documents presented in court. We are not allowed to testify, nor would a statement or an error by an OTP translator or a CLSS translator be evidence. I think that goes without saying. Your Honours are professional judges.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Step by step. There's no objection related to the colour copies S394-1B. I think we agree. I think there's no objection related to S377, the English translation. Or if so, may I hear the objections, S377, English translation of the duty roster for 21 September 1993.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think we did object to the document, and we're going to stand on that objection, although it was provisionally admitted by the Court. So we'll continue to maintain our objection on the document, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And that there is no doubt it's in fact the duty roster for 21 September 1993? I have not the B/C/S version available at the moment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: We do object to 377, the duty roster of September 1993.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All right. It was, I think, already admitted into evidence but only as S377B, and this would be now 377A. And for the reasons given frequently in the past, also the English translation will be admitted and is hereby admitted into evidence as S377A. For the same reasons - I don't want to repeat - is now related to document S77. I don't want to call this Tribunal a Babylon, but in fact all the parties should be aware that due to the fact that we have to work not only in three languages but in addition we have to be aware that due to our different background, different education, different experience, different terminology, a number of additional problems arise. We have to overcome these problems and we are all aware that here and there problems with, be it the translation or the interpretation, may happen. We all are making mistakes. And therefore if any mistake in the translation is identified, I think it's not only the right; it's even the duty for the party being aware of such a mistake immediately to draw the attention of the Trial Chamber to this mistake, and we would do so in return, no doubt in any event we identify, any mistake in the translation, and as you may have seen throughout the hearings, when it's identified a maybe mistake by the translation -- by the interpretation, that we try to do our very best and in the past all the parties did their very best to have it clarified immediately. And I think we should continue in this spirit of cooperation not only including the parties, the Judges, but also including the work of the booth, because they were of extreme assistance correcting themselves, sometimes giving us advice that a word could be translated this way and that way, and I think we should continue this way. If the Defence so wants, we can no doubt mark this newly presented document S77 in the revised translated form, mark it as S77A-1, and it will be reflected from the transcript and it should be mentioned in the list of exhibits that it was discussed and the origin of this document was discussed in -- today in open court. Objections to this procedure?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No, Your Honour. But Ms. Karper tells me that there is a "-1" a 77-1.

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: There is a B-1 but not an A-1.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. So let's call it S77A-1. And then we have both documents available and both admitted into evidence. Hereby admitted into evidence. Any other problems?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour. I have two other issues, if I may. One relates back to what the Court previously stated. And I'll try to be brief. I just want clarification with respect to Exhibit S377A. Why is it relevant a document that has a duty roster of individuals one year after the parameters in the fourth amended indictment? As the Court very well knows, the indictment is from April 30th to September 30th, 1992. This is a duty roster from September of 1993. We don't need to argue it. I just want to make sure that my objection is on the record specifically in connection with that document. In addition, I have a second request that I'd like to be heard in private session.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May we go step by step. First, submissions to this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: I would remind -- I believe the witness testified in closed session. But Your Honour, the document was admitted weeks ago. I don't think it's proper to make an objection now weeks later. We have to move forward in this case and not go backgrounds. I think the relevance is obvious. I could argue it, but Your Honours have already ruled on it.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think there is no good reason for this. But in order to avoid a theoretical approach to this, I think we were flexible enough to the past to accept as evidence documents being totally out of the framework, be it in 1990. You asked questions related to -- yes, already 1980, if not 1945. We had no problems, and we didn't stop the Defence when asking questions on 1997, 1998, or the Prosecution asking questions on this. I think it really assists us in understanding of the entire case, and it can't be done on the basis limiting ourselves only to -- for this concrete period of time reflected in the fourth amended indictment. So, therefore, nothing has to be said in addition to this, but it's quite right and I think it's a fair point for the Defence because in our guidelines on the admission of evidence, it reads that either aproprio motu or on request of one party a decision on the admission of evidence may be reversed. So, therefore, it's a fair point, but I think it's no reason -- no good reason, no good cause has been shown for revising our previous ruling on this. But for the second point now, let's please go into private session that we can discuss the second point.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good afternoon, Mr. Vila. Please be seated.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Hopefully we can conclude your testimony today. So, therefore, let's start immediately. Please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Once again, good afternoon, Mr. Vila.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would like the usher to provide the witness with the documents numbered D3, S180, and one unmarked document we submitted yesterday to all the parties.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vila, you have three documents in front of you. Can you please find the statute of Prijedor Municipality, dated 1991, work material.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: As you can see, at this Tribunal we only work with drafts. This is a draft of the statute. So can you please tell us whether this draft was ever published in any of the Official Gazettes of Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is obligatory after the statute is adopted by the assembly to publish it in the Official Gazette of the municipality. Now, whether the editors' board or a publishing committee did this with this particular document, I don't know. However, the text published in the Official Gazette must be identical to the wording and the original text adopted by the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Could you please be so kind and turn to page 3. Heading number III. Can you please read the title.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Roman numeral III: "The rights and duties of the municipality."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article number --

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Article number 7.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and turn to the following page and look for item 6.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please read out item 6, all three bullets.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6 --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we proceed, may I ask the Defence to provide us with the entire Official Gazette 7 of 84. We have before us only page 1, and 11, 12, 13 to 15, and then 61.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We were kindly provided with copies of the whole document by the OTP yesterday. We have it in our locker, and we'll provide Your Honours with the copies during the first break. These extracts are only for your use to easier follow, because we'll address only certain points in this -- from this Official Gazette. So if you agree to continue only with this partial document.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And just to inform the Court, this document was 65 ter number 1. So it may be possible to get a copy in court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's quite clear what you intend to do. Therefore, I think it's necessary to have an extremely short break that we have 65 ter number 1 in its entirety before us.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, we gave out seven copies yesterday, and I think Mr. Cirkovic will be coming back shortly with those copies for everyone.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Our case manager just left. He'll be back.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps Mr. Lukic can go to another area.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would it be possible for you to first cover another area and that it's easier for us to follow and -- and maybe it's even more successful for you if we can follow what you're trying to prove and to point out on the basis of this, comparing the draft evidently with that what is reflected in the Official Gazette. So I would appreciate if you could cover another area first and then this Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, this is the only area I have to cover. But five-minute break would help probably everybody.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The trial stays adjourned until the documents have arrived. --- Break taken at 3.08 p.m.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for giving us a chance to follow the proceedings.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: You're very welcome, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Mr. Vila, we are now on page 4 of the work material, draft of the statute of Prijedor Municipality. Will you please read item 6 of Article 7.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 6, first bullet: "Regulate and organise National Defence." Second bullet: "Facilitate the realisation of the rights and duties of citizens in connection with the defence of the country. And the third one: "Manage Territorial Defence and Civil Protection."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Therefore, this statutory provision says that among the rights and obligations of the municipality are also the management of Territorial Defence and civil protection.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: This provision speaks about National Defence, but it does not envisage that the municipal assembly should exercise any control over any of the armed forces belonging to the Ministry of Defence or the army.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it does not envisage any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would now like to ask you to please open number 65, item 1. If the usher could please help you with this.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Official Gazette from 1984, number 7, Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At the time the assembly was still operating and you were a member, it is quite obvious that this statute was not valid because it envisaged three chambers for the assembly, a tricameral assembly, whereas the assembly that you belonged to as a member had only one chamber it was a unicameral assembly. Isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: We're only trying to use this document to show what this statute envisaged, in terms of the rights and duties of the municipality. These pages are not in numerical sequence, so please if you could look for page 206. That's actually the second page of the batch. Can you please look for the heading that says "Part two," and if you could please read the title out.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Part two reads: "Rights and duties of the municipality and how to exercise them."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The first article in part two is Article 14. So if you turn to the next page, please read out item number 16.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Item 16 reads --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Excuse me, please. Article 14, before the obligations are listed, begins with -- can you please read the first part of the sentence.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Number 14, before that, "Regulate relations in residential and communal spheres." And then item 14.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now item 16, please.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: 16: "Establish and organise National Defence and protection in accordance with the system of All People's Defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: There has been a slight mistake in the interpretation, so I'll read this out again myself. Article 14: "In the municipality, item 16, establish [Realtime translation read in error "English"] and organise National Defence and protection in accordance with the system of All People's Defence." And Article 16, could you please read the first word of Article 16 in the upper right corner, "The municipality," and then item 11.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "Regulate and organise defence and protection in accordance with the system of All People's Defence within the framework of its rights and duties established by the constitution and laws."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Mr. Vila. Just a moment, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honours, I apologise. But in -- on the page 23, line 5, it reads: "In the municipality, Item 16, English and organise." And should read "In the municipality, item 16, establish organise."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Correct. I think this is one of the points that would be automatically corrected, but no doubt you are right. It reads "establish."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vila, can you please turn to page 223, heading number 4. And could you please slowly, because you've never seen this document before and we haven't spoken about this document, could you please read out the whole number 4, slowly. The heading is "All People's Defence, chapter IV." But please slowly so that the interpreters have time to finish the interpretation and also to give yourself time to familiarise yourself with the contents of this statute of Prijedor Municipality from 1984.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chapter IV, "All People's Defence, Article 140." "Within the framework of its rights and duties and in accordance --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Stop. As indicated previously, we try to follow. And could you please indicate in the English version where to find it. For example, on page 71, I read Articles 140 to 159, crossed out, and I'm apparently in the wrong chapter.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In English version, Your Honour, it's page 61.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And I would see on page 71. If you could compare it, what we -- at least what we have before us as a draft translation. Here it reads: "Chapter IV: All People's Defence." And then it reads, "Articles 140 to 159 are crossed out."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In B/C/S version, it says, "Article 140," and it's visible that on -- in the English version, on the page 70, the last paragraph is 139 and the next one on the 71 page should be 140, and obviously by mistake it's entered here "160."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I have the impression that we have different documents before us. You have another English translation. You have the final translation, and we all have the draft translation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I just learned that the witness is reading out on the basis of D3 and not S1 -- 65 ter 1. Sorry.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In our partial document, which we submitted yesterday, probably final translation - it's not draft. And on page 61 it says also "Article 140."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, that's right. But --

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: So probably we'll be able to sort out this discrepancy after.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Apparently it will be able -- we will be able to find out what is the problem, and maybe there is indeed opposed to the draft translation, we receive during the break a final translation, so -- but please continue. We are aware. Are there any comments given by the Prosecution on this?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No. Just that Your Honour is correct. Apparently these are two different translations. Sorry about that. I don't believe a final translation has been done, but we'll double-check that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Okay. Proceed, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] My apologies to you, Mr. Vila. It is sometimes necessary in the course of the proceedings to clarify certain things regarding the translation or interpretation. So will you please now be so kind as to read to us chapter IV.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Chapter IV: "All People's Defence or all National Defence, Article 140: Within the framework of its rights and duties and in accordance with the constitution, the law, the National Defence system, and the fundamentals of plans and preparatory measures for the defence of the country, the Municipality shall regulate and organise All People's Defence in its territory and harmonise and martial the preparations and organisations of associated labour, local communes and self-management communities of interest and other self-management organisations and communities. And in case of an attack on the country, organises and administers All People's resistance." Article 141: "In accordance with the system of All People's Defence, plans of larger social and political communities, the Municipality shall organise and prepare the Territorial Defence and civil defence, mobilise all available forces and resources and create material and other conditions needed for the defence; perform tasks relative to the military service and mobilisation and other legal obligations for the requirements of the armed forces; carry out preparations and ensure the training of working people and citizens, organisations of associated labour, local and self-management communities of interest, and other self-management organisations and communities of the municipal organs, authorities, and organisations for their participation in the armed struggle and other forms of resistance when protecting and rescuing the population and material assets and in the course of performance of other tasks of interest for the defence of the country." Article 142: "The organisations of associated labour and other self-management organisations and communities shall have the right and the duty to organise and prepare themselves for the all national defence in case of aggression; to independently and at the request of the Municipality and larger sociopolitical communities making full use of all potentials and available resources to ensure conditions for wartime production and other public services; to organise and implement the protection of people and material assets from combat operations and other risks; devise defence plans laying down the basic tasks, measures, and procedures at the time of an imminent threat of war and in war; provide funds to finance the preparations and perform other tasks of interest for the defence of the country." Next paragraph: "In the local communities, the working people and citizens shall organise themselves directly, prepare and train to participate in resisting the aggressor, protecting and rescuing the population and material assets from combat operations and also to perform other tasks of importance for the defence of the country in accordance with the constitution, law, this statute, and the municipal defence plan." Next paragraph: "The statute of the local community shall regulate the organisation and tasks for the implementation of the all national All People's Defence and self-defence, self-protection, and in particular the training of the population for defence and protection; shall regulate the organisation of armed and other forms of all national resistance, organisation, equipment, and training of the civil defence units; implementation of measures for the protection and rescue of the population and material assets; the drawing up of the defence plan, responsibility for the preparation of administrative agencies and organs in residential and other buildings in the course of preparation for All People's Defence; financing of the preparations for defence and protection and performance of other tasks as laid down by the municipality." Article 144: "The sociopolitical organisations, depending on the nature and character of their province of work, shall guide and implement ideological and political, moral, and psychological preparations, and initiate and guide political and other actions and measures of importance for the All People's Defence, and in case of an imminent threat of war or a war, shall activate their members, working people and citizens, to wage struggle and other forms of resistance to the aggressor." New paragraph: "Public organisations, professional and other associations --"

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think here we have to stop because also the document prepared by -- or produced by the Defence ends with Article 144.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: That's right. Only the witness didn't finish reading this article.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me check. Oh, yes. Right. Sorry. But this would be the -- we agree this would be the last article to be read out?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] So Article 144, new paragraph: "Public organisations, professional and other associations shall engage in training their members for active participation in the All People's Defence and in that respect shall cooperate with other organs and organisations in the preparation of the national defence."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, would it be a convenient time now for the break and to allow Mr. Vila to read this -- this head number 4 more thoroughly --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: But before we continue with this document, may I ask a question: Mr. Vila, we can read in Article 12 of this document that Josip Broz Tito is the first honorary citizen of Prijedor municipality and so on. And this is the Official Gazette from 1984, year 21. Has the statute since then changed one or several times?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, it was amended, but I do not know how many times. Perhaps it was only supplemented.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: During the time you acted as a deputy, was the statute changed or was it not -- or was there only a draft change?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In the beginning, you were asked by the Defence to read from a document, which was clearly a draft only. Have you ever seen this draft before, and was it part of the discussion -- were you involved on the discussion of this draft?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I cannot really remember whether I participated in the work of the assembly at the time when this draft was under consideration.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe during the break you can try -- I know it's extremely difficult for you ten years later to find out what is your best recollection of what happened, whether you worked on the basis of this statute printed in the Official Gazette from 1984, because no doubt, as the Defence may have seen, we are not hesitant to discuss and to admit this kind of evidence save it's no longer in force in 1991, 1992, and I doubt, especially based on, for example, this Article 9, declaring Mr. Tito as the first honorary citizen of the Prijedor municipality, whether this was in fact the actual statute. And we should in fact work only with the statute which was in force in 1992. I think this should be undisputed.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour, you are absolutely right. All we want to show with the old statute is that this draft may not have all details that the real statute has, because we don't have final version. We have only working version. And we want to show what usually was the part of this head of the Prijedor Municipality statute. So --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I can only state that the Bench would be more than happy to have the final version of the statute in force at the time we are discussing, and I'll leave it for the parties - I don't want to comment who might have the easiest access to the actual statute. But please try to assist the Chamber in finding the version you worked with when acting as a deputy in Prijedor Municipal Assembly, the basis of your own work. Maybe you yourself still have a copy of this important document and can assist us with this. But now it's time no doubt for the break. The trial stays adjourn until quarter past 4.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. May we have some additional guidance through this number of documents. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vila, have you had time to go through chapter IV of the municipal statute of Prijedor 1984?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Another detail that I think jogged my memory: I remember that I was present at a session when the statute of the Municipality of Prijedor was deliberated in June 1991. It was a draft document, and we were discussing parts of articles when we had one proposed draft and then alternative text. And I remember it was said that the alternative definitions should be removed, should be deleted from the text that would be published in the Official Gazette and to leave only the original proposed draft. On page 55 -- in Article 55, it says, "The executive body is made of the president, vice-president, and members elected by the assembly, and the alternative solution is the executive board is made of the president, vice-president elected by the municipal assembly and heads of the municipal administrative agencies as determined by the members of the executive board."

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Will you please slow down so the interpreters can catch up with you..

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I'm sorry for interrupting.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the parliamentary practice during 1994 -- and 1997, and 1997 to the end of term was there was an executive board. Article 55 was always identically enforced, which tells me that this statute is in force after all. There is yet a number of other alternative provisions which were also deleted from all the other articles by the decision of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Do you know if the final version of the statute of 1991 was ever published by the Official Gazette and which one was that? Could you help with that the Prosecution, and Defence, and the Chamber.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that the editorial board of the Official Gazette was duty-bound to publish the municipal statute and the supreme act of the municipality. However, I cannot really remember why that was not done and if it was not done, and it seems to transpire from all of this documentation that the Official Gazette never carried the final version, at least as far as I know.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Or perhaps we have not been able to lay our hands on that Official Gazette.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really cannot say with certainty.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Can we now go back to the statute of 1984. In Articles 140 and 141, one reads about the rights and duties of the municipality. And I'd like to ask you to help us with clarifying -- with shedding light on some terms. What are, in point of fact, organisations of associated labour indicated in Article 142?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If we translate it into today's terminology, an association of associated labour is a company or an enterprise.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the next paragraph of Article 142, there is mention of the neighbourhood of the local community. Can you tell, what is the local community?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The local community still in force today. A local community is an association of citizens governed by the territorial principle, that is, one village, several villages, localities, or parts of localities, neighbourhood communities.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you aware that in 1992 some aerial Crisis Staffs were formed in neighbourhood communities, in local communities?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I did not truly have an opportunity to communicate with or to see, but I am aware that in some local communities, local Crisis Staffs were set up, so-called local Crisis Staffs, and I believe that their role was the fuel supply, purchase of wheat, and some other activities falling within the province of work of the municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: In the Official Gazette itself, there is an error in numbering, so that after Article 142 we have Article 144. Article 144 mentions sociopolitical organisations. Could you please translate this term into today's parlance and tell us what are the sociopolitical organisations.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: At that time the sociopolitical organisations were parties, or rather, the Socialist Alliance of Working People as the broadest front of organised forces since prior to the elections of 1990 we had a mono-party system, communist -- or rather, the League of Communists, and the Socialist Alliance of the Working People.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I believe that the Federation of Youth also made part of that.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, yes, the Federation of Youth did, but not the trade unions.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: After Article 144 is paragraph 2, makes mention of public or social organisations.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Public or social organisations, if my memory serves me well, were some organisations or associations, such as a hunters' club or fisherman's club and other associations.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Now, will you please go back to Articles 140 and 141, where the role of municipalities is prescribed in organising the all national defence, or the All People's Defence. Article 141 says that the -- in the municipality, the Territorial Defence were reorganised and prepared and the civil defence too, and that working people and citizens -- associations of associated labour, local communities, and self-management interest communities too. Can you in either of these two articles or elsewhere in this chapter see it say that the municipality is responsible for organising the army or the police for the defence of its territory?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Articles 140 and 141 do not show us anywhere that the municipality is responsible for commanding or controlling the army or the police. It is responsible for ensuring the material, technical resources, and organisation of the Territorial Defence in enterprises and neighbourhood, local communities; that is, that it's responsible for the civil defence in case of natural disasters.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Could you now please have a look at document no. S180. This is Official Gazette of Prijedor Municipality no. 2 and 1992. I would like to ask you something in connection with Article 6 -- Article 9. It's about the decision and organisation on the work of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality adopted at a session of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly on the 20th of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: For the assistance of the usher, you're making reference now to Article 6 or 9?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Article 6. Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So thank you. The English version should be shown on the ELMO, please, Article 6.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Have you read Article 6?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: [No interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Yesterday we concluded that you were not a military expert. However, if we read through the provisions of Article 7 of the statute of the Prijedor Municipality dated 1991 and the provisions of chapter IV of the statute of the Prijedor Municipality dated 1984, is it your opinion not as an expert but your personal opinion -- Article 6, which envisages the functions of the Crisis Staff in the area of defence activities, do you think that's outside the scope and competence of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my opinion, in Article 6, which envisages that the Crisis Staff can coordinate work, review issues related to mobilisation, issues related to material needs and sources for the funding of national defence and familiarise itself with the general overall situation across the municipality and to monitor the implementation of military recruitment, none of these activities shows that there is the authority to exercise command or to participate in commanding any military structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: The command responsibility, can you see any traces of any command responsibility in Article 9 of the same decision at all?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Article 9, we read that the Crisis Staff has permanent cooperation with the Army of the Serbian Republic of Bosnia-Herzegovina, with the civilian protection, and with the public security through superiors and the commanding staff of these institutions as well as through the executive board, which is an executive body. However, it's impossible to glean from this any elements of any possibility of commanding any military structures or participating in the command over or of any military structures.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: For my part, we are finished now with this particular area of questioning, but I do have one further question. You told us that the Radical Party which Dr. Stakic belonged to was not the same Radical Party as Vojislav Seselj's Radical Party. Are you aware that the exact name of the party is National Radical Party Nikola Pasic? If you don't know, feel free to say so.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one correction. We think that the name of the party shouldn't be National Radical Party, but People's Radical Party Nikola Pasic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think this is one of the agreed facts between all participants in this Trial Chamber. Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Are you familiar with the fact that Muslims and Croats were members of this party too?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I did hear of that. In Prijedor, when the party was originally established, Muslims were members of the party too, and I heard from some people that Mr. Murselovic -- Mr. Murselovic's father was also an original member of this party.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: The Prosecution, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Your Honour, before I begin, perhaps we can clarify Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 11472 to 11481. that translation issue with the help of Mr. Lukic. But I know, isn't it correct that, the word narod could be translated as either a people or nation or nationality?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: "Nacionalna means "national." Narodna means "peoples."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So the word -- the name of the party so we can have it in B/C/S is nacionalna?

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Narodna --

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And isn't it correctly that the word Narodna could be translated -- well, we can argue about that later as long as we have it on the record. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, do you know was Mr. Guberina and Mr. Seselj in the same party at one time?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, they were not. But I can't be certain, because both parties were originally set up in Serbia but then before the multi-party elections, they appeared in Bosnia-Herzegovina too.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You've read several articles regarding the responsibility of the municipality and the Crisis Staff for All People's Defence. This concept of All People's Defence was very fundamental in the defence plans of the former Yugoslavia; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And this concept was that in the event of war, that the entire nation, the entire country, would be mobilised so that all individuals, all businesses or economic enterprise, all public and government and political institutions could work in a coordinated manner for the war effort; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: All defence plans applied to a possible external aggression, aggression from outside, because that was the idea at the time, that if there was to be an attack, it would have come from the outside.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, thank you for pointing that out. In fact, who was the enemy in Prijedor municipality? It wasn't a foreign army, was it? It was citizens of Prijedor who opposed the takeover; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is a very complex issue, and it's very difficult to define this whole issue in just one sentence.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Let's break it down. Was the enemy within Prijedor municipality a foreign army?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Aside from the population of Bosnia-Herzegovina itself and in some cases paramilitary units, there was no other army.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: In fact, when you talk about conflict in a place like Kozarac or the 30th of May and the attack on Prijedor, you're talking about what you considered at that time an enemy who were also citizens of Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Those were armed people, distinguishing among themselves along ethnic lines in different ways. Those people had obtained weapons, and the result of that was serious conflict.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, I asked you to please answer the questions that I ask. Were they citizens of Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: One cannot know for sure or say for sure that they were all and one citizens of Prijedor.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, in fact, they were interrogated, many of them, they were arrested, and they were identified, and in fact they were all to your knowledge citizens of Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: In the majority of the cases, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, a Crisis Staff was formed, according to what you've told us, in the event of war or the imminent state of war, a Crisis Staff or War Presidency. And that is exactly the time when also the concept of All People's Defence takes hold, correct, in a state of war or imminent state of war? Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The setting up of a presidency is prescribed if the assembly is unable to operate or a Crisis Staff, if there is an imminent threat of war or a state of war.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: The statute of the Crisis Staff, which is S180, that Mr. Lukic referred to you, in Article 6 -- I don't want to read again because we've read it at least once, but it indicates that the --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's still on the ELMO.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: For example, in the second-to-last point, "that the Crisis Staff shall keep abreast of all aspects of the situation in the Municipality, essential for the waging of armed combat and take appropriate measures." Two questions, sir: How does the Crisis Staff keep abreast of all aspects of the situation essential for the waging of armed combat?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I in my capacity of deputy know, information was circulated on the political and security situation in the area. Whether there were any additional aspects, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, in the specific case of Prijedor, that would mean receiving information from people like Colonel Colic, Vladimir Arsic, Radmilo Zeljaja, who were the commanders in the army in the Prijedor area; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were commanders. And as far as I know, they were not in Prijedor the whole time. They were wherever they needed to be, so in other places too, especially later when the war became really serious.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, my question is: Wasn't it necessary for the Crisis Staff to receive information from these commanders?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I must say this again. As far as I know, it was the information on the political and security situation, and that's how the assembly was familiarised with the situation, was informed of the situation. I, as a deputy, do not know anything else about that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, yesterday we went through the assembly minutes of a session that you said you were present at where Colonel Arsic, Colonel Colic, and -- were present and briefed the assembly on the security situation; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: How, in your opinion -- the sentence I just read from Article 6 says that the Crisis Staff shall take appropriate measures after receiving this information -- do you understand this to mean that the Crisis Staff would take appropriate measures to facilitate the work of the army in conducting the war within the concept of All People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can't say for sure because I have no information regarding that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If we go to the document the Official Gazette of 1994. We have the excerpts -- I'm sorry. I'm looking for the number of that document. D...?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: It would be marked D55.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Sorry. We can't proceed with these absolutely confusing documents. Before we continue, may I ask the witness be shown -- and I really can't go in details. We have apparently two absolutely different versions of the Prijedor Official Gazette from 1984, and therefore I would ask the usher to please be so kind, put this document on the ELMO. And I don't know -- I just received it from -- I don't know from which party it came. I received it --

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: From the OTP, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. Okay. Could you please be so kind and -- I think the parties can immediately identify that's at least another copy. What can we read at the top of the page?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we have just --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: On the right-hand side?

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Can we have just a moment because we may have confused things. We're just trying to see what we've handed out. Just a moment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. But I want to proceed with this in the meantime. What can we read on the top of the page, right-hand side, over the word "Glasnik"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it says Ksenija. I think that's a name.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then when we go -- go down, it reads something like "9/85." Could you please read what we can see there.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can see, it says in Latinic script "amendments and supplements."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Amendments and supplements. And then is it correct that --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I can tell.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. That it continues "6/90"? And what can we read then after "6/90"?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I think it says "Article 16 revoked."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And we can see that Roman III is crossed out and at the side we can read "6/90."

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That probably means "1990."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So bringing this information on the top line together with this 6/90, I don't know whether you yourself - and of course you're not an expert - but maybe working on the basis of a statute to the best of your recollection, was it at that time that parts of the statute were no longer in force and, therefore, they were crossed out?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time I was not a deputy in the local parliament, and I was in no position to be in possession of any information regarding these issues.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it's your testimony that you did not work as a deputy on the basis of this concrete statute? Because when working as a deputy, one prerequisite, no doubt, is to have the fundamental documents.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I can't say for sure that at the time when I was a deputy - that's between 1990 and 1994 - that this was valid or not valid.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it would in fact not be for you when you state that you were not confronted at all with this kind of document, because in most parts whenever a article is crossed out, we find reference to 6/90 or other concrete dates. And, for example, the articles read out by you, they were also crossed out in the document I have before me. So it would be then for the parties to discuss this matter and not leave it for the Trial Chamber as a guessing game what is valid, what has been redacted in 1985; for example, on page 251, what has been redacted, and 81, same page; 90, same page. So therefore, I'm not prepared to admit anything related to this document in evidence before we have some better and further explanation and an entire final not only draft translation of this concrete version, where we have handwritten amendments in addition. And we should leave open D55 for the purpose of these documents. And I think it will be necessary to have all the versions tendered by both parties admitted into evidence and later -- but please provide us with the full translation of this document in English, and only this can form a basis of our proceedings. So please continue.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Sir, I'll move on to a different document. You were shown earlier - and I don't think it's necessary to show it again - S180 and a decision on appointments to the Crisis Staff.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It's still in the hand of the usher, S180.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Perhaps that could be put on the ELMO, page 1 of the translation --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Official Gazette 2, 92.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Let's see. Number 19 on the first page, "Decision on appointments to Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff." If we could zoom out a bit.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, under number 6 -- the first page, the sixth name. Why was Simo Drljaca appointed to the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Could you please direct the usher to the concrete page in English.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Yes. It's the first page, I believe, page number 1 on the bottom, page 1 of the translation. Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: That's it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, why was Simo Drljaca put on the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Obviously that this number, Simo Drljaca, chief of Prijedor Public Security Station, he's appointed a member. What is the real reason, I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, wasn't it a fact that the Crisis Staff made many decisions that impacted upon the work of the police?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The list shows that certain activities and decisions, conclusions, orders of the Crisis Staff were being put through, and that includes activities requesting information from the police in relation to this or that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Well, sir, didn't the Crisis Staff set up the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I really have no knowledge if the camp was established by the army, police, or any -- or which other structure, because in no document, in no meeting, communication could I get such information, and I really do not know.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: You were an elected member of the Prijedor Assembly who continued in the assembly after the takeover, and you don't know who set up the Omarska camp?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: What I know certainly is that the Municipal Assembly of Prijedor never took a decision or verified somebody else's decision to do that, at least not at the sessions that I attended.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: So would it be correct, sir, that you don't know what decisions were made by the Crisis Staff that were never sent to the assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Apart from the information and material considered at assembly sessions, I as a councilman, I was not privy to other information.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, in answer to Judge Vassylenko's questions about work assignments, you mentioned a body of the Defence Ministry, and you also mentioned that body at another point in your testimony when talking about mobilisations for the army. If you look at the document in front of you, you will see number 7 - pointing to the Crisis Staff - is Slavko Budimir, secretary of Prijedor's Municipal Secretariat for People's Defence. Is that the local branch of the organ that you were speaking about, responsible for mobilisations?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've already said, and I will repeat it, that the Ministry of the Army at the municipal level is responsible for setting up defence departments, and they are tasked with the call-up and provision of materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Are you saying, sir, that Mr. Slavko Budimir was not responsible for mobilisations? That wasn't the work of his Secretariat for People's Defence?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, following the order of the minister and the proclaimed level of mobilisation, he sent out summons to military conscripts in the area, and that is what others in other municipalities did identically.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, in yesterday's transcript on page 46 of the LiveNote, line 17, beginning the question on live 15, you were asked: "In the period between April and September 1992, did you ever hear of the existence of a body named Crisis Staff?" You answered: "Yes. During a session of the assembly. I think that it was in late May, towards the end of May 1992, during a session of the assembly a so-called Crisis Staff was set up." I won't read further unless anyone requests me to. You were also shown a document, the one that's still on the ELMO in front of you, which indicates that the Crisis Staff was set up in the first -- the beginning of this article states, at its meeting of 22nd May, 1992 Prijedor Municipal Assembly, and then some quotations to the law, adopted the following decision on appointments to Prijedor Municipal Crisis Staff. In fact, sir, the Crisis Staff existed before -- excuse me. I believe that date -- before that decision; isn't that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I heard about the Crisis Staff and its establishment, heard first as a councilman because it was one of the items at the assembly's session.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: When did you hear that the Crisis Staff was established?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Well, when the assembly decided to organise the Crisis Staff, at a later meeting of the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was the Crisis Staff a body that coordinated within the concept of All People's Defence the conduct of the armed conflict in Prijedor in coordination with the army and with the police?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: To my knowledge, as a councilman and according to other information, a ministry department and its representative on the Crisis Staff is responsible for the mobilisation of men and the materiel, and the public security and its chief are responsible for the protection of people, public peace and order, and materiel.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Was the Crisis Staff itself, did it have responsibilities for mobilisation within Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The mobilisation is laid down by statute, and that is how it is carried out. The chief of the department for army matters receives an order from the Minister of the Army ordering to carry out the mobilisation up to a certain percentage, and that is -- and they act upon it. So there is an entire structure which is responsible for it in the department of the Ministry of Defence. As far as I know, 15 to 17 professionals work there -- I mean worked there in the previous period and at the time under consideration, and at that time that we are talking about the head was Mr. -- its chief was Mr. Slavko Budimir. When I say "its chief," I mean its head.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Sir, if you'd please answer my question. If you don't know the answer, you can say you don't know. I gather from your answer that your answer is no, but let me repeat the question. Did the Crisis Staff itself have responsibilities for mobilisation within Prijedor municipality?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Was the Crisis Staff responsible for issues as to the status of deployed forces in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not understand what you mean by "the status."

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Did the Crisis Staff issue -- was it responsible for disarming -- for the disarmament of paramilitaries?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Could the witness be shown S60.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: While that's being prepared, sir, I understand you indicated you never attended any meetings of the Council for National Defence for Prijedor. Is that correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wasn't present.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: If you could please take a moment and look at the minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council of National Defence of Prijedor Municipality held on the 15th of May, 1992. Sir, the individual responsible by law for presiding over the Council for National Defence of Prijedor is the president of the municipality; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am not sure.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Thank you. Sir, the minutes in front of you indicate a list of persons attending. Among those persons are Vladimir Arsic, Pero Colic, Radmilo Zeljaja, and all three of these were members of the military; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Also in attendance was Slobodan Kuruzovic, who at that time was the head of the Serbian Territorial Defence, the Serbian TO; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: He is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And also in attendance was Simo Drljaca, who was in charge of the police in Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: And the agenda of this meeting indicates that the organisation that the National Defence Council discussed organising the Crisis Staff, mobilisation, and the municipality, the status of deployed forces, disarmament of the paramilitary formations, and taking over the duties of the military department. Do you have any reason to believe that this organisation with these individuals did not discuss these issues on the 15th of May, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I was not in a situation, nor did I know who was on the Council for All People's Defence or what they did.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay. Thank you. And you testified that the law provided that only the assembly could establish a War Presidency or Crisis Staff. But this document indicates that the formation of the Crisis Staff was decided by the National Defence Council on the 15th of May, before the assembly met after the takeover; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The assembly was not aware of it, nor was it informed about it when the establishment of the Crisis Staff was proposed to it.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: As a member of the assembly, do you believe it is the responsibility of the president of the assembly, who is also the president of the National Defence Council, to keep the assembly informed about events of importance in Prijedor?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The councilmen should have been told that.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: Okay.

utterances.speaker: MR. KOUMJIAN
utterances.text: No further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Your Honour, just one short question regarding this document.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
