utterances.text: May I just stay with this. I'll give you the floor immediately, and maybe in reaction to this question you can be even more concrete.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yesterday's testimony, LiveNote page 49, line 1 through 3. When asked did you participate in the meeting of 22nd of May, 1992, you said, "I said yesterday that I am not sure that I attended this session, but I said that I was at the session at which decisions, orders, and other conclusions were ratified." Maybe when thinking back to -- on what you have testified yesterday there was some assistance that you could refresh your memory whether or not you participated in this meeting of 22nd of May, 1992.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... on the composition of the Crisis Staff. Today on page 47, line 6, you answered -- line 6 -- "I heard about the Crisis Staff and its establishment, heard first as a councilman because it was one of the items at the assembly's session." So to the best of your recollection, when did you hear as a councilman that this was one of the items of the assembly's session?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot say with certainty, but there is no doubt that I must have learned about it not later than the time when the conclusions and decisions of the Crisis Staff were being adopted. I do not say -- I cannot say -- I am not quite sure whether I learnt about it before that from the Official Gazette, because the Official Gazette is not delivered specially to councilmen.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Isn't it true that an agenda was distributed before the meeting of the municipal assembly started, and was it sent to all members of the municipal assembly?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: As a rule, the agenda is delivered to councilmen earlier, but very often all the accompanying material is not being sent along, apart from a note saying that the necessary papers will either be distributed at the session itself or reasoned out at the session itself.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So would it be consequent to expect that on an agenda for a assembly meeting to come, one could read "establishment of a Crisis Staff," and then "composition of the Crisis Staff"? We have to make a distinction between the meetings the 20th of May, 1992 and then the 22nd of May, 1992. Could you please answer and not only nod, because it's not reflected on the transcript when you are nodding only.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. I wasn't quite listening. I've lost concentration. Could you repeat the question, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was: Wouldn't it be consequent then that there was an agenda in preparation of the meeting of the 20th of May indicating that on this agenda one, if not the only point, was establishment of a Crisis Staff and then as a follow-up, the next meeting, 22nd of May, a composition of the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: The invitation, I presume, said "Decision to establish Crisis Staff." But the draft agenda did not contain the decision or the next one, which spoke about this composition, that is, the item on the agenda is the composition of the Crisis Staff. But I'm quite sure that the invitation to the councilmen did not say who would be those individuals.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This would mean that you received an invitation prior to the meeting 20 May 1992 indicating, as you said, decision to establish Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Wouldn't this be such an important issue on the agenda that you felt necessary to participate in these extraordinary times in the session of the municipal assembly? I just want to refresh your memory whether you maybe had personal impediments, obstacles depriving you from participating in this extraordinary, important meeting of the assembly or based on this you come to the conclusion that you participated, in fact, in both meetings.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am really trying, but I cannot remember whether I was present in the assembly.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So would it be a correct conclusion you were confronted with a -- with the minutes of the fourth meeting of the Council for National Defence of the Prijedor Municipal Assembly held on 15th May 1992, then prior to the meeting of the 20th of May you received an invitation indicating that one item or one issue of this meeting was the establishment of a Crisis Staff? Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. That we hopefully can finalise this round of questions now, but of course it's for the parties to decide themselves. Two other areas where I didn't have a final certainty based on yesterday's transcript. You told us on page 47 of LiveNote transcript line 6 through 9 that you yourself participated in the ratification of the previous orders. You said, "Yes, but I must say that these were just the title of these orders, decisions, conclusions without their contents." My question now as a follow-up would be: Did you ever request when you had the impression that the one or other decision, conclusion, or order seemed to be of some importance for you, did you ever request to see the underlying entire document?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot remember if either I or any other councilmen asked for that.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Were you ever aware that maybe -- or did you verify whether all orders, decisions, conclusions of the Crisis Staff were included in this document, only as you told us by the title?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So it would be possible that there would be orders, decisions, conclusions of the Crisis Staff not mentioned in this document?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you regard it as a mistake and a breach of rules of the municipal assembly if there were such orders, decisions, conclusions not included in this document but nevertheless taken by the Crisis Staff?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there was any such thing, it must have been a mistake.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And a final area. With the assistance of Defence counsel, we found out yesterday that, as you testified previously, that in the case of the absence - I make reference to LiveNote page 37, lines 11 through 18 - you testified that in the absence of Dr. Stakic, it would be for Mr. Savanovic to sign on behalf za Dr. Stakic. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then we found out with the assistance of Defence counsel that in fact we were confronted with two documents where we could read in writing "Dr. Milomir Stakic" but then later on not a signature which seems to be or which could be a signature of Mr. Savanovic. What was the rule? In the absence of both Dr. Stakic and Mr. Savanovic, who would be the competent person then to sign?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No third person would have had the authority to sign. This would not have been legal for any third person.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So whoever signed this document would have acted illegally?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You were not asked yesterday whether you could by chance identify one of the signatures you saw with the za under the typed name of Dr. Milomir Stakic.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think I can glean the point of your question from the interpretation I have received.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was: You saw yesterday two documents where apparently there was a signature under the typed name "Dr. Milomir Stakic" that without any doubt were not the signatures of either Dr. Stakic or Mr. Savanovic. My question was: To the best of your recollection, did you by chance identify one of these signatures you saw?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I was not able to identify either of the signatures. I am not familiar with those signatures.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So this would conclude my questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: So, please, Mr. Lukic.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: I would just like to clarify something regarding the last document the Prosecution showed the witness. It's document number S60. So could the usher be so kind and show the witness this document.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You do have the document before you, Mr. Vila, don't you? Down the middle of the page, top of the page, first we see minutes of the agenda and then the first thing we can see is "Conclusion. Will you please tell us -- will you please read for us the conclusion itself, what the conclusion was. Just the first paragraph, please.

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: "The draft of the decision on the organisation and functioning of the Crisis Staff is approved under the proviso that a representative of the garrison in Prijedor be added to the proposed list of members of the Crisis Staff."

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Will you please now take document S180, which is the Official Gazette of Prijedor municipality number 2/92. Turn to page 37. I wish to ask you something about the decision on appointments to the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality. On page 37, there is a list of people who were appointed members of the Crisis Staff of Prijedor Municipality. Among these people who are listed here - there are ten people altogether, ten names - do you recognise anyone from the Prijedor Garrison?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: By adopting this decision, does the adoption of this decision mean implementation of the decisions from the Council for National Defence of Prijedor Municipality or not?

utterances.speaker: CEDOMIR VILA [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. LUKIC
utterances.text: Thank you. I have no further questions.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Let me ask all the participants. Any further questions to this long testimony to be added? I can't see any. Thank you, Mr. Vila, for following this journey through a jungle of documents, and I wish you a safe trip home to your home country and your home town. Thank you. And the witness may be escorted out of the courtroom, please.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Thank you very much, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Before we have the short break, the Trial Chamber has discussed the issue of whether or not to continue the hearing on Monday, the 10th, and we can't see any possibility to vacate the decision to continue the trial Monday, the 10th of February. And we took into account that it was scheduled to have a hearing the 10th and 11th of February, and no doubt it takes at least ten days of preparation, and we are convinced that the Defence was and still is prepared to have a witness to be called for the 10th of February. And in addition, we would ask the Defence also to take care that a witness will be available on Friday, the 7th of February. Maybe a witness covering two days that we could hear this witness February 7th or February 10th. Please let us know before the end of this hearing what your intention is, how to proceed, because it would be then for us to take the necessary steps to proceed with the hearing and the hearing in this case. The trial stays adjourned until 6.00 sharp.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Please be seated. I thought Defence counsel wanted to answer immediately when standing up.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, thank you, Your Honour. We're grateful for the opportunity to address the Court again. In connection with this issue, we tried to contact our investigator in the field and were unable to do so. However, we will endeavour to bring a witness so that we could fill those days as requested by the Court. Right now we can't tell you with any certainty who the witness is and whether or not that will be accomplished, but you have our confidence as officers of the court that we will endeavour to bring another witness so that we can complete the day on Friday, as well as Monday, February 10th.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you for this cooperation, and we would appreciate whenever possible to let our legal officer know when you know exactly that you have a witness available and who this will be. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: May I then ask the usher to escort the next witness into the courtroom. Any protective measures not announced until now?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Vuleta. Can you hear me in --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Good afternoon.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Can you hear me in a language you understand?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, I can, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Would you please be so kind and give us your solemn declaration.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I solemnly declare that I will speak the truth, the whole truth, and nothing but the truth.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. You may take your seat. And as it's a Defence witness, the floor is for Mr. Ostojic. Please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Good evening, Mr. Vuleta. As you know, my name is John Ostojic, and along with Branko Lukic and Danilo Cirkovic, we represent Milomir Stakic. I would ask, sir, that you state for the record your name and your surname.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Cedo Vuleta.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Would you be kind enough to move your chair a little closer to the mike, to the microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: [The witness complies]

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May you give us your date of birth.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The 15th of July, 1958.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, where do you presently reside?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I reside in the village of Srednja Maricka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us in what municipality that village is in.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: In Prijedor municipality.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, what is your ethnic background?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I'm a Serb.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In the spring and summer of 1992, where did you reside?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I resided in Maricka.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The same village as you do presently in the municipality of Prijedor; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I still reside in the same village.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us briefly your educational background. Where did you go to school, when, and what degree did you obtain?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I went to elementary school and completed elementary school in the village of Maricka and my secondary education in the village of Prijedor. And after that I studied -- I studied electronics, electrical engineering.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Are you, sir, an electrician as a tradesman?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: No. I am an electrician working for the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: When you referenced the Omarska mine, you're referring to the iron ore mine that's located in the town of Omarska; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us how long you've worked at the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I have worked for the iron ore mine since mid-November 1984 and to this very day.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just briefly, if you can, tell us where you worked prior to being employed at the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Prior to my employment in the Omarska iron ore mine, I was working in Split in a shipyard. And after that I worked in Zagreb for the city trams.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During both those tenures of employment, in what capacity were you employed?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I worked as an electrician, and I was in charge of electrical production lines and electrical equipment.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell us if you have any military service.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I did my regular military service from the 11th of March, 1977 at military post 7225 Pula. I was in the marine artillery. To -- I can't remember the exact date, but it was in June 1978.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If we can focus a bit on your tenure in your present employment at the iron ore mine from mid-November 1984 through the present. Can you describe for us your general duties and obligations and in essence your day-to-day work that you perform at the iron ore mine during those significant years.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: While the iron ore mine was still operating and while production was ongoing in the iron ore mine, I was working on maintenance of BTO systems and other electronic equipment and installations in the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, were you also responsible during this time period for maintenance of generators and water pumps as well?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes, I was responsible for that too.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Describe for us, if you will, how it is that an electrician or a man with your area of specialties is involved with the water pumping system and the generators in an iron ore mine so that we can have a better appreciation of what it is you do.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I don't think I quite understand the question. What you want me to explain? Will you please try to rephrase the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'll try. When you discussed the water pump at the iron ore mine and the water pumps that are there, they're generated and the output or the pressure of these water pumps is generated through electrical currents and electrical conduits; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes. I worked on water pumps, water pumps pumping water from the depth of up to 180 metres, and the water pumping stations that would spout surface water. The iron ore mine is essentially a deep pit between 150 and 200 kilometres in depth and about a kilometre across, so that's where the iron ore was dug. The pumps were supposed to throw all the water from the inside out all the time. There were many mining machines, diggers, conveyer belts, so the water had to be pumped out, because if the water wasn't pumped out, the whole production lines underground would be flooded.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And it was, sir, your job responsibility throughout this period of 1984 through 2003, to the present, to ensure that there was a water supply and that the system with respect to the water supply operated appropriately and regularly in the iron ore mine; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes, that's correct.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, this water that is being brought into the iron ore mine through these water pumps and generators, as you've described them, that water was utilised for what purpose, sir?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The water would be pumped out of the mine and then through the water pipeline, the water would be led to the river of Gomjenica.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you tell us how prior to 1992 water at the iron ore mine was being brought there for people who were employed to drink or to use the facilities, namely the bathroom facilities. How would they accomplish receiving water at the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: That's a different story altogether. The iron ore mine got its drinking water from a special water well containing drinking water which was located in Donja Lamovita. The village of Donja Lamovita was between 5 and 6 kilometres from the mine. There were deep water pumps there pumping the water out and throwing the water into a basin, into a pool in Gradina, near the church, and then potable drinking water would flow down the same way back towards the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, correct me if I'm wrong. Part of your responsibilities at the iron ore mine was to make sure that there was drinking water at the specific complex, correct, to be used by visitors, employees, et cetera?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd like to focus your attention, if I can. In the period of 1992, did there come a time in 1992 that you recall, sir, that the iron ore mine that you were employed ceased to work or stopped working?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: That's right. The mine stopped working when Prijedor was attacked.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I know it's been a long time since 1992. I think we've established that that date was approximately, or I think it is, May 30th, 1992. So just so that I'm clear on your testimony, is it your testimony that the iron ore mine ceased working and ceased operations after May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: That's right. The mine ceased working, and the mining section stopped.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Did you, sir, continue following May 30th, 1992 through approximately August 5th, 1992 -- did you continue to go to the iron ore mine because you were compelled to do so under a work obligation?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I stayed on in the mine. I was under work obligation. That was my combat order.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: As you sit here, sir, do you recall if there were any changes to the physical structures of the iron ore mine prior to May 30th, 1992 that you would have personally observed after May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: No, no change took place, nothing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me ask you with respect to the interior structures. Did you notice, sir, whether or not there were any changes to any of the interior structures that are located on or at the iron ore mine, meaning from prior to May 30th, 1992 and subsequent to May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Nothing changed. Everything stayed the same.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, were there any external changes, modifications, or alterations to the iron ore mine complex prior to May 30th and after May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: There were no changes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, did you, to the best of your recollection and based upon your personal experiences and observations -- when was the next time after the iron ore mine complex stopped working that you were present at the iron ore mine? Was it immediately on May 30th, a couple days later, a couple weeks later? What was it?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Well, a few days later.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Could you describe for us, sir, what it is that you saw and observed those couple days after May 30th, 1992 when you found yourself at the iron ore mine.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: When I got there, after the 30th of May, I noticed that prisoners had arrived in the Omarska mine.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: During that time period, sir -- and just so that we can concentrate and focus on the time period. Since the iron ore mine ceased working after the attack on Prijedor, and we could fix that as a date for our purposes, May 30th, 1992, up until the time that the detainees in the investigations centre were released, approximately August 5th or thereabouts, in early August 1992. My question to you for that time period, sir, is: What were your job duties and obligations from May 30th through the beginning of August 1992 at the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's necessary to have a breakdown of this long and winding question, because it may be confusing for the witness. And for these purposes, is it your own recollection or is it on the basis of the leading questions put to you by the Defence that in fact you would fix the date for May 30th, 1992? That would be the date when the iron ore mine ceased working after the attack on Prijedor. Is this the correct date? Is this your own recollection, or could it be slightly different?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I do not recollect the exact date. It was late May. But I kept no record, so I can't know the exact date.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: And then when exactly was it that you were mobilised, that you were ordered to work in the iron ore mine?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Well, I worked there before. I simply went on working there, except that I was issued with a document, with a paper, which said "labour work obligation."

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just to be quite clear, because it seems to be important from the outset to know about the exact time frame. It would be incorrect if I would ask you did -- you were mobilised to work at the Omarska camp in May -- already in May of 1992? Would this be incorrect or correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I worked there without interruption. I just -- I simply went on working. And when people arrived to the centre -- and later on I was issued with a paper, with a document that I would not be sent to the front but that I should be on duty there and maintain the electrical equipment.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think then we have a clear picture of that what is your testimony on the time frame. I apologise for having interrupted you, but I think from the outset it should be quite clear what period of time we are exactly discussing. Please proceed, Mr. Ostojic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you, Your Honour. And if I may just for the record -- I'll refer to the witness's prior transcript. I believe the Court has on page 7450. In response to a question with respect to the issues that we're discussing -- the answer on line 3 -- and again, for the record I'd like to read it -- from this witness was, "I don't know the exact date. I don't remember. I know that the mine was functioning when the war was going on in Croatia. As soon as Prijedor was attacked, it stopped functioning." Lines 1 through 5.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All right. Maybe --

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it seems we've got different transcripts. I'll speak with the Defence when we finish this evening, because I've got a final transcript and it's not on that page.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Yes. Therefore -- maybe the problems we have in the moment emanate from the fact that we, in fact, have two different transcripts. And I can't follow your; maybe you couldn't follow my question, so --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Perhaps, your -- and quite candidly I was just trying to facilitate the process. And if it was a leading question, it was as a result and reliance upon this. I'd be glad to show the Court through the registrar or usher specifically that page and that transcript relating to Mr. Cedo Vuleta. The Presiding Judge at that time was the Honourable Judge Rodrigues. I'd be happy to tender that to the Court.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: This is once again an agreed fact. Could the usher perhaps help --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I apologise for the markings on this page. This is just a work --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I hope they are in English that I can read them. Yes. Apparently we have two different versions, and therefore I apologise also for you. The line of questioning may have confused you, but you know that you testified already in 2001 and we have two different paginations. And my reference was to the question when you were mobilised to work in the iron ore mine. But let's come back to this when we have both the same copies of documents. Please proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I will try. I'm trying to just focus the questions, if I may, for this time period.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And sir, forgive us for this interruption and thank you for your patience. From the time that you recall that you began your work obligation at the iron ore mine, I think as you've stated, after the attack on Prijedor, how long did you continue to work at the iron ore mine under this work obligation that was issued to you?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I was under the work obligation until 1995, when Sanski Most was attacked, when there was fighting in Sanski Most. That is when I was taken away from there and I joined a unit.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: The detainees that were brought in the iron ore mine after the attack on Prijedor that you personally saw, how long did they continue to stay at the iron ore mine? From what period to what period?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The detainees stayed there -- as a matter of fact, they arrived towards the end of May and stayed there until the end -- or until late August. I cannot pinpoint the date or the day because I kept no record of any such thing.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So we'll work with your period.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, counsel, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If possible, we'll work with your period, the same time period that you're referencing. Did you, sir, continue to work under your work obligation at the iron ore mine on a regular and continual basis?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I went on working regularly, without any interruptions until 1995, when I was called up. And then I stopped working.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you share with us, once again, to the extent now that we have clarified the time period, that is, up until the time the detainees left -- during that time period, can you tell us what your job duties obligations were? Meaning from late May, early August, through late -- strike that. Let me restate the question, Mr. Vuleta. I know it's late, and I apologise. Sir, can you describe for us your job duties and obligations from the time that the detainees came to the iron ore mine up until the time that they left the iron ore mine. What were your job duties and responsibilities?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: My duties and responsibilities were -- that is, my task number one was the maintenance of the well, supplying us with the drinking water. Then the lighting, the lighting around the buildings, the administrative building, the dumping truck building. I was also -- worked with the pumps, with the pumps pumping out, be it ground waters or surface waters in the mine. Oh, and I forgot, and I also maintained the kitchen, or rather, the equipment in the kitchen.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us whether you worked an eight-hour shift - again, focussing solely on that time period while the detainees were at the iron ore mine - did you work an eight-hour shift, twelve-hour shift, or twenty-four-hour shift?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I worked -- I would work 24 hours, and then have 48 hours off. That is, I'd be on duty for one day and then have two days off.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And during your job duties and obligations and responsibilities at that time, did you ever leave the complex to perform some of your functions in order to go, for example, to the well where the water pumps and generators were operating?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Every day, day in, day out, it was my duty to go around the pumps, pumping out surface waters. Then I was also under duty to see to the kitchen equipment, because at that time there were frequent power cuts. So that I had to switch on the generator, which was in the heating plant near the kitchen, next to the separation plant.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you tell me, during that time period, sir, to whom did you report?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: During that period of time, my superior was Mirko Babic.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Also during this time period, sir, were there other employees of the iron ore mine who had worked prior to May 30th at the iron ore mine that were also under work obligation after May 30th, 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Why, there were. Other people, people working with pumps, Branko Rosic, Zdravko Bjelobrk. There were women, I mean cooks in the kitchen. There were the guards, all the security men, mine security people. And well...

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: You briefly discussed the external and internal physical structures of the iron ore mine as well as the external premises of the iron ore mine. My question to you now is: Was there a change with respect to people being present at the iron ore mine compared the period prior to May 30th and after May 30th of 1992? Was there in addition to the detainees other people who were at the complex?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I don't really understand the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Let me try it a different way, with the Court's permission, and of course the consent of the OTP. After May 30th - if I may ask a leading question - after May 30th, was there any evidence of a police force or policemen being present at the iron ore mine during the period of time that the detainees were present?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Oh, yes, naturally. Why, there was police when the detainees came and there was police there and the army troops were around. I mean, you were talking about the mine. I didn't understand.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In addition to the police that was present after May 30th, 1992, was there any other group or entity that was present in addition to the work -- the employees who were under work obligation, the detainees that you mentioned, and the police that you mentioned just now? Was there any other entity?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes. There was a unit belonging to a Banja Luka formation.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And I think you mentioned in your answer also army troops; correct? As reflected on line 17, page 31.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With the Court's permission, if the usher can show the witness or place on the ELMO S15-2. Just so the record is clear, where he mentions this is on page 71, line 13, as opposed to -- as reflected in the transcript, line 17, page 31, for whatever it's worth.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, you're being shown a picture of a model that was used by the OTP, I believe, of the iron ore mine or parts of the iron ore mine. Do you recognise the picture that's on the ELMO identified as S15-2?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I do, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Does that picture and the model reflect the iron ore mine in its entirety?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: No. Here we see only the administrative building and the canteen and the dump truck garage, and behind it is the workshop where bulldozers were repaired and then the white house, where workers were usually roll called or checked in. And then I also see the warehouse for oils, lubricants, some fuel, I think. And then the water reservoir.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: In respect to the exhibit that's before you - although, I don't believe that this is S15-2, but it's close to it - can you tell me whether or not there were any posts, electrical posts or flower beds or shrubs on or about the complex in 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Around -- all around was public lighting.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: So there were the utility poles which illuminated light when a switch was turned on; correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: There were quite a number of lampposts. All around were the lampposts.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Was there anything else other than lampposts on or around this area? We, I think believe or we can agree that there was grassy area or field on or around that area. Was there an entrance and an exit to the iron ore mine that you can show us as reflected on the picture that you're looking at?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: I don't understand. Entrance? What do you mean? The access to these buildings, or ...?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: That's a perfectly appropriate response. My question was a bit vague, and I apologise for that. In order to enter the complex, the iron ore mine complex, how would you enter it? From which direction?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The mine was entered from east.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: And was there a road that led up through that entrance?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: There was a road. The road came from east, from the direction of Omarska.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Now, you mentioned the cafeteria. To the best of your recollection, during the time period that the detainees were at the iron ore mine, can you tell us where this cafeteria is as reflected on this exhibit before us.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: It is here, in this area.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'm going to attempt, Your Honour, just for the record to clarify those two points that the witness described. First of all, the entrance the witness describes to the iron ore mine, I believe that he indicated it was the area while facing the picture. There seems to be a building to the right, and it's towards the bottom, viewing this south, of the building approximately. And next the witness indicated that the area which is the cafeteria is directly perpendicular from where the entrance is and across the building at its other end. So if I may proceed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Can you describe for us that building that you're facing that's on the right -- describe for us what during the spring and summer of 1992, what was in this building?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Before the detainees arrived you mean? Is that what you want me to explain?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Before the detainees arrived, this was the office, the administrative building, this part here. Over there was the canteen, the workers' canteen. Here was a garage for passenger vehicles. I mean, the manager's and executives' who worked in the mine. Here we had lockers and bathrooms or changing rooms and bathrooms. There was an entrance here, so inside here was a passage that you took in order to get to the canteen over there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Maybe it could be of assistance for your purposes if we made use of S15-19. Of course, it's for you to decide whether based on this document it might be easier. If the usher could show S15-19 to the Defence, please. Only that we need not return to this.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: With -- absolutely, whatever the Court suggests. But there is a purpose for which we'd like ultimately to show this exhibit as well as S15-2.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: All right.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd be more than happy to proceed in accordance with the Court's instructions. Yes. So please place -- yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Witness, you now have before you another document, which is marked S15-19. Can you describe for us what that is.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can maybe assist the witness, Your Honour, with all due respect.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, this, I believe, is another model prepared by the OTP without the actual roof showing the inside of the --

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: This is the same building, but this is the ground plan.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: All right. It's actually an aerial view purportedly of the various rooms within - just bear with me - within the structure that we were talking about which appears on S15-1, the structure to the right where the administration building or offices were and where the cafeteria was. Correct?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Looking at this, to the best of your recollection, is this a fair and accurate depiction of the breakdown of the rooms within that building that we were just discussing, which is on the right side of S15-1?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: This doesn't seem identical to what I remember the building as looking like.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Well, let's just --

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: There's a cafeteria here, but the entrance to the cafeteria is not here, so I don't think this is a fair rendering of the building.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Let me just -- if I can further assist you, Mr. Vuleta. If you take Exhibit S15-1. And if you could just take --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Is it S15-1 or 2, Mr. Usher?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. S15-2, the picture we have there is actually reversed from the model that has the aerial view. Okay. So it's reversed. So just take a look at the two again, and just help me identify the various portions of the building. See, in S15-2, when you look at it on the right, the administration building is the first thing that you see, and then the cafeteria. Whereas, when you look at the exhibit before you, S15-19, it's actually reversed. The cafeteria seems to be the first thing that you look at at the bottom of the page and then going north you would see the administration building, I believe. Before you answer, I think we have a concern from our learned colleague.

utterances.speaker: MS. SUTHERLAND
utterances.text: Your Honour, it may assist the witness if he can see S15-18 first and then look at 15-19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: If the parties can agree on this procedure.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I'd be happy to show the witness that exhibit, Your Honour, as well.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Mr. Vuleta, you have now before you yet another exhibit. Just -- just describe that exhibit to us. What is it that you see, sir? I'm trying to move this along.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: This here is the cafeteria and the administrative building. So this is, I think, a fair rendering of the whole complex. And the image that I was looking at before, that was sort of reversed.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. Taking that picture, sir, and with the Court's suggestion, looking at the aerial view, is it still your testimony that the aerial view photograph does not accurately depict the inside rooms as they existed in the spring and summer of 1992?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: This image here, this model, does not reflect what the building is really like, or the breakdown of the rooms. This is where the cafeteria was and --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If you could show us --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: If I can just move along.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: We should have it on the transcript. The witness is referring at this moment to Exhibit number S15 --

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. If I can -- would the Court just like me to describe that it's the northern portion that the witness was indicating in his last answer, and indicating basically that in the centre of that northern section of the aerial view of the photograph on Exhibit S15-19.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: When we just have -- I apologise. But that we do not need to come back to this -- all these pictures. May I ask you: Where was the entrance to this building? Can you identify this on this document?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Yes. On the document that's on the ELMO, S15-19. Correct, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Where it reads -- could we please zoom a little bit in. I can't read the number of -- in the area where there is room number -- is it 36 or 26? Unfortunately I can't read it. I should have stronger glasses. To the left-hand side. It should -- 26. Is it correct, 26, 27 that there was the entrance? Correct?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] No. This -- I don't seem to understand this model that I'm looking at. There is no corridor here. This is all closed. There are no doors, and there should be a corridor here to walk through and then you proceed towards the cafeteria and then up to the first floor.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: You are speaking about a cafeteria. This was a cafeteria that was used by the inmates, or was it for the purposes of staff members, the cafeteria?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I think, Mr. Vuleta, that was directed to you, that question. So if you could just answer the Court's question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The entrance was here, and then you came this way, and this is where the cafeteria was. But this is a reverse image. So that's why I'm confused.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In fact, maybe it can be of assistance to show the witness document S15-19 in addition.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I just -- I just think that it seems that we're regressing. Just so that we're clear -- if I may, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just to indicate for the record where this witness on this S16-19 aerial photograph, where he indicated was the entrance. And that, if I may, he indicated it was at or approximately what is marked as -- it's difficult to read, but it's the centre right-hand side of the picture, which has a pink slip showing "A" and then a number that we can't see unless it's zoomed further. It looks like it's approximately in the area that the witness identified is the area marked as A18, and to the left, looking at --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This entrance. This.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: [Microphone not activated]

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for the Presiding Judge, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Thank you. And Madam Registrar just found out that it may in fact be of assistance to show the witness S15-19 as well?

utterances.speaker: THE REGISTRAR
utterances.text: -3, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: In addition to the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: May I put the question to the witness, Your Honour?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Of course. Of course.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Sir, now you have before you an exhibit that's identified as S15-3, I believe. Can you describe first for us what that picture purports to be.

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Here you can see the actual -- the faithful reflection of the cafeteria with the administrative building. This is exactly where the entrance was, but it wasn't like that in the other image. This is where you came in. And here were the offices of the administration. This is where the garage was, and this part here was the cafeteria. And I think this very faithfully reflects what the building was actually like.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Thank you for your assistance. Before we break for the evening, the Court did, I believe, ask you a question that we did not get a response to. And that is, sir: With respect to the cafeteria that you mentioned and identified, during the spring and summer of 1992 was that, sir, the cafeteria where the detainees were brought to eat as well as the workers at the iron ore mine ate?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Will you please help me along with this. The detainees were not brought here before the end of May. Only the employees, the worker, were actually there.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Okay. I'll break it down. Prior to May 30th, 1992, was that the cafeteria that the regular employees at the iron ore mine would come in and sit and eat during their regular lunch breaks or during their break periods?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: Yes, yes, yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: After approximately May 30th, 1992, while the detainees were at the iron ore mine, do you, sir, know where those detainees would eat?

utterances.speaker: CEDO VULETA
utterances.text: The detainees ate in the same cafeteria.

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: Just so the record is clear, the witness pointed to the area where he previously identified as the cafeteria on Exhibit S15-3.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: Just to conclude this, was there any special room tailor-made for staff members, investigators, or other personnel, maybe for the purposes of breakfast or lunch or dinner only?

utterances.speaker: MR. OSTOJIC
utterances.text: I believe, witness --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: It was my question now. If I may ask you, was there any additional room especially -- during this period of time especially for staff members, investigators, typists, secretaries, where they would take breakfast, lunch, or dinner?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I understand your question. There was yet another restaurant with the kitchen attached to it near the separation, 2 kilometres to the east, where all the food was prepared. This cafeteria, ready and prepared food was brought here and then it was distributed.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: My question was: In that same building we can see now on our computer, in this same building was there another room for having lunch, breakfast, or dinner for members of the staff, for investigators, for typists, or whatever persons working there?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I don't know. I didn't really enter those buildings very often, or I didn't spend much time where the offices of the investigators and the typists were. It's possible that they do have a room upstairs somewhere which they used to eat in, but I know that there was this restaurant with the kitchen, and I know that the investigators usually went there to take their lunch.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
utterances.text: I think it's appropriate to have the break now. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow. But before we take the break, let me kindly ask you not to contact in the meantime one of the parties, be it the Prosecution, be it the Defence, or Judges, or whenever you meet another maybe witness in your hotel. Please don't discuss issues related to your own testimony. Thank you for your understanding. The trial stays adjourned until tomorrow, Friday, at quarter past 2.00.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE SCHOMBURG
